title: AND, OR and NOT: combining tests

screens.prompt: In B9, answer TRUE only when the total is over 100 and every item has at least 15 units.

hints.syntax: =AND(test 1, test 2): the answer is TRUE only when both tests are.

docs.syntax: =AND(test1, test2, ...) needs every test; =OR(...) needs one; =NOT(test) flips it
docs.explain:
AND, OR and NOT take logical tests and return a single TRUE or FALSE. AND needs every argument to hold and OR needs one, while NOT flips the value it is given. Each argument is normally a comparison, though a bare number counts as TRUE unless it is zero.

On this sheet the total is 150 and the smallest item is 18. Both tests in =AND(B8>100,MIN(B2:B7)>=15) hold, so the cell answers TRUE. The second screen asks whether any item is under 20 or the total is over 200, and Bolt's 18 settles it on the first test alone.

Most mistakes here come from choosing between AND and OR. On data like this either function answers TRUE, so a wrong choice stays hidden until a month when the two tests disagree.

errors.text: An argument is text where a logical test belongs, as when a word reaches AND without quotes.
A function name is mistyped, so no test runs at all.
A formula holding a single comparison looks complete but skips the second condition, so a short item still passes.

docs.atWork: Marking a month for restock only when the stock total is low and one line has run short.
docs.outcome: Combine several tests into one answer, and choose AND or OR to match the question.
docs.teaches: AND and OR over comparison arguments, and what a bare number argument means
docs.dataset: Stock list with a total row and a smallest item
